context: Hypothetical sales study. A local cinema is considering two emails for school organizers who have inquired about a weekday group screening. Each email offers the same available dates and price. The public sources describe comparable buying situations. The outreach and offers are invented.
question: Would the organizer request a date hold by email within two business days?

arms.pay_at_request: A weekday group screening costs $240 for 20 seats. Reply with a date to hold it for 48 hours. The $100 nonrefundable deposit is due at the time of your request and is credited to the $240 total.
arms.pay_at_confirmation: A weekday group screening costs $240 for 20 seats. Reply with a date to hold it for 48 hours. The $100 nonrefundable deposit is due when you confirm at the end of the hold and is credited to the $240 total.

cases.source: P.S. 748 PTA minutes, May 1, 2025, p. 1, June Field Trip. Brooklyn, NY. Records a planned sponsorship; payment terms and booking outcome are unknown.
cases.evidence: A parent association plans to sponsor a movie-theater outing for grades 3–5. At the meeting the date has yet to be determined. The available information does not establish a spending limit, authority to pay a deposit, or the date the organizers must decide.

cases.source: Issaquah School District, Field Trips FAQ, expenses and sources of funds, accessed 2026-11-25. Washington state. Describes an institutional rule; the organizer and proposed screening are hypothetical.
cases.evidence: Consider a trip sponsor working under a process that requires an expense and funding plan to submit a field-trip request. The totals must match. Whether this organizer has secured funds or may place a free hold before approval is unknown.
